effects: Exactly `assets` USDC moves from the signer to the vault (safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)); it uses the signer's existing USDC allowance to the vault.
figrUSDC vault shares are minted to `onBehalf`. The number is previewDeposit(assets) at the current share price after interest and fees accrue, with no minimum.
If a liquidity adapter is set, the deposited USDC is then allocated to it. This is vault-internal and does not change what the signer gets.
formats.shown: Deposit 1 USDC for <onBehalf>, with the share token named as figrUSDC and the share recipient labelled 'Send shares to'.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted is not shown, and the contract has no minimum-shares input.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The share count comes from storage (totalAssets, totalSupply, fees), not calldata. The descriptor only shows a 'Share ticker' constant.
findings.fix: None possible from calldata. The ticker field already names the share token.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' raw constant field is a separate line that only shows 'figrUSDC'.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json deposit field {"label":"Share ticker","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker"}; case 0 screen shows 'Share ticker: figrUSDC'.
findings.fix: Optionally merge it into the recipient label, e.g. 'Send figrUSDC shares to', and drop the separate field.

cases.notes: The signer's only effect is 1 USDC out, shown as 'Deposit asset: 1 USDC'. The 1e18 figrUSDC shares went to 0xdEaD (signer null), which the screen states and the reader understood.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: figrUSDC shares are burned from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up, at the current share price, with no maximum.
Exactly `assets` USDC moves from the vault to `receiver`.
If msg.sender != onBehalf, the share allowance that onBehalf gave the signer goes down by the shares burned (unless it is unlimited).
Interest and fees accrue first (accrueInterest), which sets the share price used.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 100 USDC to <receiver>, with an 'Owner' field naming onBehalf. Nothing says shares are burned or how many.

findings.title: withdraw: the figrUSDC shares burned from the owner are not on the screen. Their amount comes from storage.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)` → exit(): `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. Case 1 mined: 99.327662074199227350 figrUSDC out from the signer, and no field shows it.
findings.fix: The amount can't come from calldata. Name the share token in the intent or labels, e.g. intent 'Withdraw USDC (burns figrUSDC shares)'.

findings.title: withdraw: the 'Owner' label does not say that figrUSDC shares are burned from that address.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json withdraw field {"path":"onBehalf","label":"Owner"}; code exit(): `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)` and allowance spend when msg.sender != onBehalf. Case 1 reader: 'Whether any shares or receipt tokens get burned from my wallet. The screen doesn't list them.'
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Burn figrUSDC shares from' and/or add onBehalf to the interpolated intent: 'Withdraw {assets} from {onBehalf}'s figrUSDC to {receiver}'.

cases.notes: 100 USDC in to the signer is shown right. The 99.33 figrUSDC burned from the signer is not shown at all. The reader guessed their position goes down but was unsure whether shares are burned.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: USDC moves from the vault to `receiver`. The amount is previewRedeem(shares), rounded down, at the current share price, with no minimum.
If msg.sender != onBehalf, the share allowance that onBehalf gave the signer goes down by `shares` (unless it is unlimited).
Interest and fees accrue first, which sets the payout rate.
formats.shown: Redeem 30292.89661312329825533 figrUSDC to <receiver>, with onBehalf labelled 'Owner'. Neither the asset received nor its amount is named.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names USDC as the asset the receiver gets.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit(): `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = USDC (immutable 0xa0b8...eb48). The descriptor redeem fields are only shares/receiver/onBehalf, and constant underlyingTicker goes unused. Case 2 mined: 30504.265302 USDC in to the signer. The reader wrote 'likely USDC, amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field, e.g. {"label":"Receive","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}, or say it in the intent: 'Redeem {shares} for USDC to {receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is not shown, and the contract enforces no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. The amount comes from storage (share price) and there is no minAssets parameter. Case 2: 30504.265302 USDC received, not on the screen.

findings.title: redeem: the 'Owner' label does not say the shares are burned from that address.

cases.notes: 30292.896... figrUSDC out is shown right. The 30504.27 USDC in to the signer is implied by 'Redeem ... to' but its asset and amount are not stated.
